tweets.text: Grok @Bot can be your personal chief financial officer!

quoted.text:
I literally hooked up ALL my finance accounts to Grok Bot. 

I really mean all of them:

1/ Chase
2/ Charles Schwab
3/ E*TRADE
4/ Fidelity
5/ Robinhood
6/ Wealthfront
7/ Apple Card
8/ 𝕏 Money

FYI, this is a total of 30 accounts... Chase alone is 13 accounts between checking, savings, brokerage, credit cards, a 401(k), trusts, a stock plan, and 529s for the kids.

I was already honestly the best with my $ money and I’ve NEVER made a late payment in my life. But before Grok Bot, I was wasting so much time bc every answer lived in different apps. Like my cash was in one place, cards in another, brokerage accounts somewhere else, and had to compile everything in a spreadsheet, if I even got around to putting it together.

Now I just text my Grok Bot CFO.

I can ask, “What’s my cash right now?” and it pulls everything together and separates personal from business. I can ask which credit cards are coming due and whether I have enough cash to pay them all in full. Green means I’m covered, red means I’m short, and it tells me exactly how much I need. I actually tested this... going red on purpose. Like I moved $ money around so I would come up short on one of the upcoming bills, and Grok caught it.

I can even ask, “Where did my $ money go?” and instead of opening a bunch of apps, downloading transactions, cleaning up a spreadsheet, and making a chart myself, it pulls everything together and gives me the breakdown.

Today, I also asked it for a pie chart of all my stock investments with the amounts and percentages. 

1/ TSLA is 84.9%
2/ SPCX is 10.4%
3/ NVDA is 4.7% 

That’s across $ money sitting in different brokerage accounts, and it's awesome that I didn’t have to think about where any of it was. 

I literally just asked it one question... you can see for yourself. 

If you’re serious about your finances, you already ask the same questions all the time. 

• Like, can I cover everything that’s due? 
• Where did my $ money go? 
• How much $ cash do I really have? 
• What investments do I actually own? 

But honestly, the annoying part is that your financial life is usually scattered across 10+ different apps/platforms and a bunch of accounts, so getting a real answer takes a lot of work and your time. And honestly, most people probably don’t even look until something feels off or if they get a notification that a payment was missed or something.

Now, with all my finance accounts linked, I just ask a normal question, Grok Bot checks everything it has connected, and gives me the answer. Then I can ask the same thing tomorrow, and again whenever, and get the updated version without rebuilding anything.

The fact that you are able to talk to your entire financial life like you’re texting someone who already knows where everything is... this is a total game changer in the world of finance imo. 

If you really care about your $ money, hook yours up to Grok Bot. 

It's so worth it.

1. A Chief of Staff who opens the day pulling open loops from email & t…

retweet.text:
Things my @bot setup does that still blow my mind:

1. A Chief of Staff who opens the day pulling open loops from email & tasks and suggesting things it can knock out before 7am.

2. After every meeting, decisions get folded into Notion, Linear, and Todoist — not left rotting in Granola

3. Every email starts as a draft. The CoS bot scans my email every ~2hr and drafts replies to nearly everything — including checking my cal for availability and finding requested attachments / links

4. A specialist for each lane: curriculum, engineering, coaching, hiring, content, ops, and one for every single piece of software

5. Routines that keep running while I’m offline (e.g. monitoring Sentry errors in our apps and proactively fixing things)

6. Group rooms where 2–4 bots share one project thread instead of me copy-pasting context

7. Cloud coding agents that pick up Linear issues and open PRs after running the list of open work by me EoD — then squash-merge to main when it’s done

8. Meeting prep briefs pulled from Granola + Notion before I walk in

9. A growing shareable knowledge base in Notion + a GitHub repo that we update daily based on what happens at school

10. Student progress look-up across Expertise, Followers, and CoFounder without inventing numbers — chat anytime to see where a student is on their business work

11. Mentor Mind that coaches me on how to hold the bar without inventing doctrine

12. Todoist as a central task list where it logs things it’s blocked on for me, or from meetings / emails — and I can paste links into chat to direct it how to solve them

13. Engineering work is automatically tracked in Linear so my and the product teams’ bots don’t collide with each other

14. Presentations spun up in Gamma / Claude Design without me opening a slide tool

15. Plaud / live capture → notes the bots can actually act on

Probably more but these were the immediate ones we thought of.

Michael Nicolls just just laid out SpaceX's ambition for connectivity that extends beyond Earth

“We will connect the Moon with a constellation, and then we will connect Mars”

"Our goal, again, is to extend consciousness beyond this planet, and we want to go and connect the Moon and Mars

But before that on Starlink, we're creating the technologies to connect the Moon with very high-bandwidth connectivity systems, very high-bandwidth lasers

And we will connect the Moon with a constellation, and then we will connect Mars, and we will form an interplanetary mesh of connectivity that is fundamentally driven by the same technologies we're working on with Starlink

To make this happen, SpaceX needs to keep improving safety in LEO so everyone can operate and scale safely”

Build safe, coordinated infrastructure in LEO first then extend connectivity and human presence to the Moon, Mars, and beyond
